tools.name: validate_geodata
tools.description: Check whether a dataset's DECLARED coordinate reference system actually describes its own coordinates, before you draw it on a map. Catches the failures that are otherwise silent: swapped lat/lon axes, degrees labelled as metres, and Web Mercator or another projection mislabelled with a UTM or national-grid code. Pass the declared CRS (e.g. "EPSG:4326") and a sample of the raw coordinates as {x, y} in the dataset's OWN units, deliberately not named lon/lat, because whether they are degrees is the question. Returns a verdict (consistent / suspect / impossible), what is wrong in plain language, and where the numbers actually point when read another way. This is a sanity check, not a reprojection: it never transforms coordinates. Local computation: no network call, no quota.

XY.description:
One coordinate from the dataset, in the dataset's own units, NOT
necessarily degrees. Named `x`/`y` rather than `lon`/`lat` precisely
because whether they are degrees is the thing in question.

coordinates.description:
A sample of the dataset's coordinates. A few dozen is plenty; the
check is about ranges and spans, not volume.

declared_crs.description:
The CRS the dataset claims, e.g. `"EPSG:4326"`, `"EPSG:32610"`,
`"EPSG:3857"`, `"EPSG:27700"`.

tools.name: verify_places
tools.description: Check whether places (and itineraries) an AI mentioned are real, findable and physically possible. Pass structured `claims` (reliable, and the only path that supports itinerary feasibility) or free `text` (best-effort quoted-phrase extraction). Each claim resolves to exactly one of three verdicts, never a boolean: "verified" (matched a real place, with its stable id and the source/date of the evidence), "contradicted" (a specific, dated, sourced fact rules it out, currently only an itinerary leg the routing engine proves cannot be driven in the stated time, with the computed travel time as evidence), or "unverified" (no evidence either way). This tool NEVER asserts that a named real business does not exist or has closed, that would be a defamation risk with no upside; a missing match is always "unverified". Claims sharing increasing `sequence` values and both carrying `claimed_time` (ISO 8601) form itinerary legs checked for feasibility via `matrix`, catching e.g. "breakfast in Bath, 10am meeting in Edinburgh". Max 20 claims per request. A claim takes only `id`, `name`, `locality`, `sequence` and `claimed_time`; any other field (e.g. `near`) is refused naming the accepted ones, so put disambiguating context such as a town in `locality`. The response's `summary` field is a concise plain-text digest (also returned as this tool result's text content) so clients that drop structured/non-text content blocks still see the verdicts.

CostingKind.description:
Costing models exposed by the MCP tools (a deliberate subset of the
Valhalla costing list), serialised in snake_case exactly as Valhalla
names them.

oneOf.description: Standard car costing.

Truck costing; honours dimensional limits and, when a `truck`
profile is supplied, ADR dangerous-goods restrictions.
Bicycle costing; tune it with a `bicycle` options object.

Pedestrian (walking) costing; tune it with a `pedestrian` options
object (lit streets, wheelchair/blind, hiking difficulty).

Motor scooter (moped) costing: like auto but prefers lower-speed
roads and may use ways closed to larger motor vehicles.

VerifyClaimInput.description:
One place claim for the `verify_places` tool: a place an AI mentioned,
to be checked for existence and (as part of an itinerary) feasibility.

Unknown fields are refused, naming the accepted ones. A dev-lane run
(19 Oct 2026) passed `near` instead of `locality`; it was silently
dropped, "Roman Baths" matched Ankara, and the itinerary leg became
uncomputable with nothing telling the caller why.

claimed_time.description: ISO 8601 timestamp: when the itinerary claims you are at this place.

id.description:
Caller-chosen id, echoed back on the matching result. Auto-assigned
("claim-1", …) when omitted.

locality.description:
Optional disambiguating context, e.g. "Oxford". Country-level words
("UK", "England", …) are stripped before querying, they add noise,
not signal, to name search.

name.description: The place name as claimed, e.g. "The Eagle and Child".

sequence.description:
Itinerary position. Claims that share increasing `sequence` values
and both carry `claimed_time` form legs the feasibility pass checks.

claims.description:
Structured claims, the reliable path, and the only path that
supports itinerary feasibility. Mutually exclusive with `text`.
Max 20 per request.

text.description:
Free text to extract place claims from (best-effort heuristic:
quoted phrases and Title Case runs after "at/in/near/to/from/
visiting", not NLP or an LLM call, and it does not attempt
itinerary feasibility since there are no explicit times to anchor
legs to). Mutually exclusive with `claims`. Max 8,000 characters.

tools.name: weather_along_route
tools.description: Forecast weather along a route, each sample read for the hour you actually reach it rather than the weather right now. Pass the route's `shape` (an encoded polyline6, the `route` tool's geometry_polyline6), optional `depart_at` (RFC 3339, default now), the route's `duration_s` (from `route`; omitted, an 80 km/h average is assumed and `duration_source` says so) and optional `sample_interval_m` (default 25,000, 5,000 to 100,000, at most 40 samples). Each sample carries its ETA, temperature, rain, snowfall, precipitation type and probability, wind and gust speed, visibility, the WMO weather code and `severe` (thunderstorm and heavy precipitation codes only). It is a FORECAST, not an observation: read on a 0.05 degree grid (about 5.5 km) at the nearest hour, up to 16 days ahead, and samples past that horizon or without data come back `available: false` with a reason, never painted dry. `summary` is one sentence (where rain or snow starts and for how far, the strongest gust, samples without data) and always ends by saying it is advisory, never a routing guarantee: keep that qualifier when you pass it on. Requires the MapMap gateway; a deployment without a weather source answers a clear error. Display the returned `attribution` with the forecast, linked to `attribution_url`, with `licence_url` (CC BY 4.0) linked; `derived_fields` names the sample fields MapMap derives rather than Open-Meteo supplies.

depart_at.description:
Departure time, RFC 3339 (e.g. "2026-10-12T14:00:00Z"); defaults to
now. Forecasts reach about 16 days ahead; samples past that answer
unavailable.

duration_s.description:
The route's duration in seconds, used to work out when you reach
each sample. Pass the `route` tool's duration; omitted, a generic
80 km/h average is assumed and `duration_source` says so.

sample_interval_m.description:
Distance between samples in metres (default 25,000, clamped to
5,000 to 100,000; at most 40 samples per route).

shape.description:
The route shape as an encoded polyline6 (the `route` tool's
`geometry_polyline6`).

tools.name: weather_frames
tools.description: The NOAA GFS forecast frames MapMap publishes for drawing weather on a map: 17 frames (0 to 48 hours every 3 hours) of the newest run, each with URLs for the global rain, temperature, cloud, gust and sea-level pressure PNG fields (1440 by 721, value-encoded; decode with `encodings`), the wind field (PNG plus JSON ranges) and XYZ tile templates for rain, temperature and isobars. Optional `run` (YYYYMMDDHH) and `fields`. The URLs need the caller's own MapMap key. A FORECAST, not an observation, processed by MapMap from NOAA GFS 0.25 degree data (regridded and quantised): never describe it as original NOAA data or imply NOAA endorsement. `status` says whether the newest run is fresh. Requires the MapMap gateway. Display the returned `attribution`.

fields.description:
Which fields to return URLs for, any of `rain`, `temp`, `cloud`,
`gust`, `mslp`, `wind`, `isobars`. Default: all.

run.description:
A forecast run as YYYYMMDDHH (UTC), e.g. "2026101700". Default: the
newest run.
